translationRepairs: When the soldiers Huangfu Hui and others mutinied, they tried to make the commander Yang Jing their leader. Jing refused and was killed by the mutineers, who then brought his head to force Zaili to lead them.

When the soldiers Huangfu Hui and others mutinied, they tried to make the commander Yang Zheng their leader. Zheng refused and was killed by the mutineers, who then brought his head to force Zaili to lead them.
The name graph 晸 is Zheng, matching the accepted person record, not Jing.
It happened that the soldiers Huangfu Hui and others mutinied, pushing the commander Yang Jing as leader; Jing did not comply and was killed by the crowd, who carried Jing's head to coerce Zaili.
It happened that the soldiers Huangfu Hui and others mutinied, pushing the commander Yang Zheng as leader; Zheng did not comply and was killed by the crowd, who carried Zheng's head to coerce Zaili.
The literal field repeats the same misreading of 楊晸.
When Gaozu took the throne, Zaili was transferred to Yanzhou, given the additional titles of acting Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
When Gaozu took the throne, Zaili was transferred to Yunzhou, given the additional titles of acting Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
鄆州 is Yunzhou; it differs from the earlier 兗州, Yanzhou.
When Gaozu ascended the throne, Zaili was transferred to garrison Yanzhou, with the added titles acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
When Gaozu ascended the throne, Zaili was transferred to garrison Yunzhou, with the added titles acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
The literal field likewise must distinguish 鄆州 from 兗州.
In the seventh month of the sixth year of Tianfu he was appointed military commissioner of Xuzhou.
In the seventh month of the sixth year of Tianfu he was appointed military commissioner of Xu Prefecture.
Xu Prefecture unambiguously renders 許州 without leaving Chinese characters in ordinary English prose; the later 徐州 remains Xuzhou.

When Quanjie first took office at the Ye capital, he went in white robes to the county court of Yuancheng, his home district, to pay his respects. The magistrate Shen Xun drew back in embarrassment and would not accept the gesture.

When Quanjie first took office at the Ye capital, he went in white robes to the county court of Yuancheng, his home district, to pay his respects. The magistrate Shen Gou drew back in embarrassment and would not accept the gesture.
沈遘 is Shen Gou, not Shen Xun, in both translation fields.

When Quanjie first took the Ye capital post, because Yuancheng was his native district he put on white robes and went to the county court to pay respects; the county magistrate Shen Xun hesitated and avoided him, not daring to receive the courtesy.

When Quanjie first took the Ye capital post, because Yuancheng was his native district he put on white robes and went to the county court to pay respects; the county magistrate Shen Gou hesitated and avoided him, not daring to receive the courtesy.
The literal rendering repeats the incorrect reading of 遘.

During the Tang Tianfu era his elder brother Yun served as guest general of Daliang's four commands. Jian traveled from Haizhou to visit him; Yun recommended him to the Yanzhou commander Wang Zan, who took him on as adjutant.

During the Tianfu era of the Tang dynasty (901–904), his elder brother Yun served as guest general of Daliang's four commands. Jian traveled from Haizhou to visit him; Yun recommended him to the Yanzhou commander Wang Zan, who took him on as adjutant.
The dynasty identifier 唐 distinguishes this Tianfu era from Later Jin Tianfu; dates clarify the reference without retaining Chinese in the translated prose.
Yang Yanxun, courtesy name Chenzhang, was a native of Baoding in Hezhong.
Yang Yanxun, courtesy name Chengzhang, was a native of Baoding in Hezhong.
The courtesy name 成章 reads Chengzhang.
Lu Siduo was a native of Linhuang in Cao Prefecture.
Lu Siduo was a native of Linhuang in Chanzhou.
澶州 is Chanzhou, not Cao Prefecture.
When Mingzong ascended the throne, Wu was made commander before the imperial tent and appointed prefect of Cao Prefecture.
When Mingzong ascended the throne, Wu was made commander before the imperial tent and appointed prefect of Chanzhou.
The office held is prefect of 澶州, Chanzhou.
Xiang Lijin, courtesy name Fengjin, was a native of Bingzhou.
Xiangli Jin, courtesy name Fengjin, was a native of Bingzhou.
相裏 is the compound surname Xiangli, followed by the personal name Jin.
Quanjie's service to the Jin house included pacifying An Chongrong's rebellion and fighting at Zongcheng. His achievements were considerable, and his honors were deserved.
Quanjie's service to the Jin house included the pacification of Anlu and fighting at Zongcheng. His achievements were considerable, and his honors were deserved.
安陸 is Anlu, while 宗城 is the separate Zongcheng campaign; the source does not name An Chongrong in the first clause.
